records.source: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
records.gloss: Not judge, so that not you be judged;
pieces: Stop passing judgment on others, so that you will not be judged.

L.1: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.

R.1: Do not judge other people, and God will not judge you.

decisions.choice: judge: condemn, set oneself up as judge over others
alternatives: make any moral judgment at all
decisions.reason: The verb covers both deciding and condemning. Jesus does not forbid telling right from wrong (7:6, 15-20); he forbids a harsh, fault-finding judgment of others that ignores one's own faults (7:3-5).

decisions.choice: so that you may not be judged: by God
decisions.reason: The passive points to God's judgment, as 7:2 shows.

decisions.choice: God will not judge you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies.

records.heading: Judging others

records.source: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: With what for judgment you judge you will be judged, and with what measure you measure it will be measured to you.
pieces: The way you judge others is the way you will be judged, and the measure you use for them will be used for you.

L.2: For with the judgment you judge, you will be judged, and with the measure you measure, it will be measured to you.

R.2: God will judge you in the same way you judge others. He will use the same rules for you that you use for them.

decisions.choice: the measure you measure: the standard you use for others
decisions.reason: The picture is of a merchant measuring grain. Jewish teachers used the saying "measure for measure" of God's justice.

records.source: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
records.gloss: Why but do you see the speck the in the eye of the brother of you, the but in the your eye beam not you notice?
pieces: Why do you stare at the splinter in the eye of {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, and never notice the beam of wood in your own?

L.3: And why do you look at the speck in the eye of {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?

R.3: Why do you notice the tiny bit of dust in the eye of {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, but you do not notice the big piece of wood in your own eye?

decisions.choice: speck and beam: a tiny fault in another and a huge one in oneself
decisions.reason: The speck is a bit of straw or sawdust; the beam is a roof timber. The comic picture shows how blind people are to their own faults while they correct others'.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, a brother is a fellow member of God's people, man or woman.

decisions.choice: a tiny bit of dust, a big piece of wood
decisions.reason: Readable describes the two things.

records.source: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
records.gloss: Or how will you say to the brother of you, Let me cast out the speck from the eye of you, and behold, the beam in the eye of you?
pieces: How can you say to {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, 'Let me take that splinter out of your eye,' when all the time there is a beam in your own?

L.4: Or how will you say to {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' and look, the beam [is] in your own eye?

R.4: How can you say to {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, 'Let me get that dust out of your eye,' when you have a big piece of wood in your own eye?

decisions.choice: speck and beam: a tiny fault in another and a huge one in oneself
decisions.reason: The speck is a bit of straw or sawdust; the beam is a roof timber. The comic picture shows how blind people are to their own faults while they correct others'.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, a brother is a fellow member of God's people, man or woman.

decisions.choice: look (L); when all the time (B); when (R)
decisions.reason: The word that points to what follows becomes a contrast in Balanced and Readable.

records.source: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
records.gloss: Hypocrite, cast out first from the eye of you the beam, and then you will see clearly to cast out the speck from the eye of the brother of you.
pieces: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly enough to take the splinter out of the eye of {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}.

L.5: Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of the eye of {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}.

R.5: You are only pretending to be good! First take the piece of wood out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly enough to help {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}} get the dust out of {{gender:their|his}} eye.

decisions.choice: hypocrite: one who plays a part, here by correcting others while ignoring one's own sin
decisions.reason: As in 6:2, the word first meant an actor.

decisions.choice: then you will see clearly: help is still to be given, after self-examination
decisions.reason: Jesus does not forbid helping another with a fault; he tells the helper to deal with his own first (compare 18:15).

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 5:22, a brother is a fellow member of God's people, man or woman.

decisions.choice: You are only pretending to be good!
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hypocrite is.

records.source: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
records.gloss: Not give the holy to the dogs, nor throw the pearls of you before the pigs, lest they trample them with the feet of them and having turned they tear you.
pieces: Do not give holy things to dogs, and do not throw your pearls to pigs. They may trample them underfoot and then turn on you and tear you apart.

L.6: Do not give what is holy to the dogs, nor throw your pearls before the pigs, lest they trample them under their feet and turn and tear you to pieces.

R.6: Do not give holy things to dogs. Do not throw your pearls in front of pigs. They will only walk on them, and then they will turn and attack you.

decisions.choice: dogs and pigs: people who scorn and attack what is holy
alternatives: all who do not yet believe
decisions.reason: Dogs and pigs were unclean animals. The holy thing may be meat offered in sacrifice. The saying balances 7:1-5: do not condemn, but do not keep pressing God's good things on those who treat them with contempt. Who is meant is not said.

decisions.choice: what is holy: food set apart for God, such as sacrificial meat
decisions.reason: Meat from the sacrifices was holy and could be eaten only by priests or worshipers (Exodus 29:33; Leviticus 22:10). Throwing it to dogs would be unthinkable.

records.source: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
pieces: Keep asking, and you will receive. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and the door will be opened for you.

L.7: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

R.7: Keep on asking God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give to you. Keep on looking, and you will find. Keep on knocking, and the door will open for you.

decisions.choice: ask, seek, knock: keep on doing so
decisions.reason: The commands are in the present tense, which can mean to go on asking. The three verbs say the same thing three ways: pray to God with confidence.

decisions.choice: it will be given, it will be opened: God will give and open
decisions.reason: The passives point to God, as 7:11 shows.

decisions.choice: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the present tense.

decisions.choice: asking God, he will give
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

records.heading: Ask, seek, knock

records.source: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
records.gloss: Everyone for the asking receives and the seeking finds and to the knocking it will be opened.
pieces: For everyone who asks receives, whoever seeks finds, and the door is opened to whoever knocks.

L.8: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

R.8: Everyone who keeps asking will receive. Everyone who keeps looking will find. And the door will be opened to everyone who keeps knocking.

decisions.choice: everyone who asks receives: God answers his children
alternatives: a promise to grant anything requested
decisions.reason: The promise rests on God's goodness as Father (7:11). It is given to disciples who seek his kingdom (6:33), not as a guarantee of whatever they want.

records.source: ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
records.gloss: Or who is from you a man, whom will ask the son of him bread, not a stone will he give him?
pieces: Would any of you give {{gender:your child|your son}} a stone when {{gender:they|he}} asked for bread?

L.9: Or what person is there among you who, if {{gender:your child|your son}} asks for bread, will give {{gender:them|him}} a stone?

R.9: Suppose {{gender:your child|your son}} asks you for bread. You would not give {{gender:them|him}} a stone, would you?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: The Greek form shows the answer expected: no parent would do it.

decisions.choice: bread and a stone: a round loaf and a stone of the same shape
decisions.reason: A small round loaf looked like a stone (4:3). The cruel trick would be to give something like what was asked for, but useless.

decisions.choice: {{gender:your child|your son}}
decisions.reason: The point is a parent's care for any child, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.source: ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
records.gloss: Or also a fish he will ask, not a snake will he give him?
pieces: Or give {{gender:them|him}} a snake when {{gender:they|he}} asked for a fish?

L.10: Or if {{gender:they|he}} asks for a fish, will [you] give {{gender:them|him}} a snake?

R.10: If {{gender:they|he}} asks for a fish, you would not give {{gender:them|him}} a snake!

decisions.choice: a fish and a snake: something like a fish that could harm
decisions.reason: Some fish of the Sea of Galilee look like snakes, and a snake was unclean food. The second picture repeats the first.

records.source: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: If therefore you evil being know gifts good to give to the children of you, how much more the Father of you the in the heavens will give good things to the asking him.
pieces: So if you, sinful as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!

L.11: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who [is] in the heavens give good things to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!

R.11: You are sinful, but you still know how to give good things to your children. So you can be sure that your Father in heaven will give good things to those who ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: being evil: sinful, even at your best
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of human beings as sinful by nature, set against the goodness of the Father. Even so, they care for their children.

decisions.choice: how much more: from the lesser to the greater
alternatives: God is like a human father in every way
decisions.reason: As in 6:26 and 6:30, the argument runs from human care to God's far greater care.

decisions.choice: sinful
decisions.reason: "Evil" in English suggests special wickedness; Balanced and Readable say "sinful", as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
records.gloss: All things therefore as many as you want that should do to you the men, so also you do to them; this for is the law and the prophets.
pieces: So in everything, treat others the way you would want them to treat you, for this is what the law and the prophets are about.

L.12: So everything that you want {{gender:people|men}} to do to you, so also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.

R.12: Do for other people everything you want them to do for you. That is what the law of Moses and the teachings of the prophets are all about.

decisions.choice: do to others what you want them to do to you: a positive rule of love
alternatives: do not do to others what you would not want
decisions.reason: Others, including the teacher Hillel, had taught the negative form: do not do to others what you hate. Jesus states it positively, as a call to act.

decisions.choice: this is the law and the prophets: this sums up the Scriptures
alternatives: this replaces the law and the prophets
decisions.reason: The phrase ties back to 5:17. Jesus says the same of the two great commands in 22:40.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses and the teachings of the prophets
decisions.reason: As in 5:17.

records.source: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι’ αὐτῆς·
records.gloss: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide the gate and broad the road the leading to the destruction, and many are the entering through it;
pieces: Go in through the narrow gate. The gate that leads to destruction is wide and the road to it is easy, and many go in that way.

L.13: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide [is] the gate and broad the road that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it,

R.13: Enter through the narrow gate. The gate and road that lead to ruin are wide and easy, and many people go that way.

decisions.choice: two ways: the choice between life and death
decisions.reason: Moses set before Israel the way of life and the way of death (Deuteronomy 30:15-19; Jeremiah 21:8). The gate may be the entrance to the kingdom, at the start or the end of the road.

decisions.choice: destruction: final ruin at God's judgment
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of life in 7:14, the life of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: easy
decisions.reason: The broad road is the easy one; Balanced says so.

records.heading: The narrow gate

records.source: ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
records.gloss: for narrow the gate and pressed the road the leading to the life, and few are the finding it.
pieces: But the gate that leads to life is narrow and the road is hard, and only a few find it.

L.14: for narrow [is] the gate and hard the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it.

R.14: But the gate and road that lead to life are narrow and hard. Only a few people find them.

decisions.choice: hard: narrow, pressed in, a road of trouble
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb for pressing or afflicting. The way of the disciple includes hardship and persecution (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: life: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: Life here is entering the kingdom (19:16-17, 29; 25:46).

records.source: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
records.gloss: Beware of the false prophets, who come to you in clothing of sheep inwardly but are wolves ravenous.
pieces: Watch out for false prophets. They come to you looking like sheep, but underneath they are hungry wolves.

L.15: Beware of the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.

R.15: Watch out for people who say they speak for God but do not. They come to you looking gentle like sheep, but inside they are like hungry wolves.

decisions.choice: false prophets: those who claim to speak for God but lead people astray
decisions.reason: Israel had long been warned against them (Deuteronomy 13:1-5; Jeremiah 23:16). Jesus warns of them again in 24:11, 24.

decisions.choice: sheep's clothing, wolves: harmless outside, dangerous within
decisions.reason: The flock is God's people; the wolves look like members of it but prey on it.

decisions.choice: people who say they speak for God but do not
decisions.reason: Readable says what a false prophet is.

records.heading: Known by their fruit

records.source: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
records.gloss: By the fruits of them you will know them.
pieces: You will know them by what their lives produce.

L.16: By their fruits you will recognize them.

R.16: You will know who they are by what they do.

decisions.choice: fruits: what a person's life produces, in deeds and in teaching
decisions.reason: As in 3:8 and 12:33, fruit is the outcome of a life. False prophets show what they are by how they live and by what their teaching produces.

records.source: μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
records.gloss: Not do they gather from thorns grapes or from thistles figs?
pieces: Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

L.16: Do they gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?

R.16: People do not pick grapes from thornbushes or figs from weeds.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The Greek form expects "no". Readable states the answer.

records.source: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
records.gloss: So every tree good fruits good produces, the but bad tree fruits bad produces;
pieces: In the same way, every healthy tree bears good fruit, and a diseased tree bears bad fruit.

L.17: So every good tree produces good fruit, but the bad tree produces bad fruit.

R.17: In the same way, every good tree grows good fruit, and every bad tree grows bad fruit.

decisions.choice: bad: rotten, diseased, worthless
decisions.reason: The word is used of rotten things. The tree's nature shows in its fruit.

decisions.choice: healthy, diseased
decisions.reason: Balanced uses words for trees.

records.source: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
records.gloss: Not is able a tree good fruits bad to produce, nor a tree bad fruits good to produce.
pieces: A healthy tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a diseased tree cannot bear good fruit.

L.18: A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.

R.18: A good tree cannot grow bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot grow good fruit.

decisions.choice: cannot: what a person is will show in what they do
decisions.reason: The saying is about recognizing what is there. Jesus elsewhere calls for a tree to be made good (12:33).

records.source: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
records.gloss: Every tree not producing fruit good is cut down and into fire is thrown.
pieces: Any tree that fails to bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

L.19: Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into [the] fire.

R.19: Every tree that does not grow good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

decisions.choice: the words of John the Baptist (3:10)
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats John's warning word for word. The levels repeat the wording they used at 3:10.

records.source: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
records.gloss: So then by the fruits of them you will know them.
pieces: So you will know them by what their lives produce.

L.20: So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.

R.20: So you will know who they are by what they do.

decisions.choice: fruits: what a person's life produces, in deeds and in teaching
decisions.reason: As in 3:8 and 12:33, fruit is the outcome of a life. False prophets show what they are by how they live and by what their teaching produces.

decisions.choice: the saying of 7:16 repeated, closing the section
decisions.reason: The repetition frames 7:16-20.

records.source: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ’ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
records.gloss: Not everyone the saying to me, Lord, Lord, will enter into the kingdom of the heavens, but the doing the will of the Father of me the in the heavens.
pieces: Not everyone who calls {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only those who do what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven wants.

L.21: Not everyone who says to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father who [is] in the heavens.

R.21: Not everyone who calls {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'Lord' will enter the kingdom of heaven. Only those who do what {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father in heaven wants will enter.

decisions.choice: Lord, Lord: calling Jesus master and lord with eager devotion
decisions.reason: The doubled word expresses earnestness. Calling Jesus Lord is not enough without doing God's will.

decisions.choice: the will of my Father: what God requires, as the sermon has set it out
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of God as "my Father" and makes himself the one whose words reveal that will (7:24).

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: Readable keeps one "Lord"; the doubling is a form of emphasis that the meaning note explains.

records.heading: I never knew you

records.source: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
records.gloss: Many will say to me in that the day, Lord, Lord, not in your name we prophesied, and in your name demons cast out, and in your name mighty works many did?
pieces: On that day many will say to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, drive out demons in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and do many miracles in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name?'

L.22: Many will say to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name cast out demons, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name do many mighty works?'

R.22: On judgment day many people will say to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Lord, Lord, we spoke for God in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name. We forced demons out of people in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and we did many miracles in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name.'

decisions.choice: that day: the day of judgment
alternatives: a day in the near future
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "that day" as the day the Lord would judge (Isaiah 2:11; Zechariah 14:4). Jesus himself is the judge (25:31-46).

decisions.choice: deeds done in his name: even real works of power do not prove a person is his
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say the deeds were fake. Gifts and powers are not the same as knowing him and doing God's will.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question claims.

decisions.choice: your name, with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The speakers address Jesus, so "your" takes the usual span.

records.source: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
records.gloss: And then I will declare to them that Never I knew you; depart from me the working the lawlessness.
pieces: And then I will say to them openly, 'I never knew you. Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who break God's law.'

L.23: And then I will declare to them, 'I never knew you; depart from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you who practice lawlessness.'

R.23: Then I will tell them, 'I never knew you. Go away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! You do what is wrong.'

decisions.choice: I never knew you: I never had a relationship with you
alternatives: I did not know who you were
decisions.reason: To know, in Scripture, can mean to own as one's own (Amos 3:2). The words were also used to disown someone.

decisions.choice: depart from me, you who practice lawlessness: Psalm 6:9
decisions.reason: The psalmist says, "Depart from me, all you workers of evil." Jesus uses the words as judge.

decisions.choice: lawlessness: living without regard for God's law
decisions.reason: The word ties back to the law Jesus came to fulfill (5:17-20).

records.source: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
records.gloss: Everyone therefore who hears of me the words these and does them, will be likened to a man wise, who built of him the house on the rock.
pieces: So anyone who listens to what I have said here and acts on it will be like a sensible {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house on solid rock.

L.24: So everyone who hears these words of {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and does them will be like a wise {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:their|his}} house on the rock.

R.24: So anyone who hears what I teach and obeys it is like a wise {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house on rock.

decisions.choice: these words of mine: the whole sermon
decisions.reason: Jesus's words carry the authority that the law had; hearing and doing them decides a person's end (7:28-29).

decisions.choice: wise: sensible, thinking ahead
decisions.reason: The word means prudent, as in 25:2 of the wise bridesmaids.

decisions.choice: will be like: at the judgment it will be seen
decisions.reason: The future may look ahead to the test of judgment, pictured as the storm.

decisions.choice: a wise {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house
alternatives: a wise man who built his house
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the comparison applies to everyone who hears, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.heading: Two builders

records.source: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
records.gloss: And came down the rain and came the rivers and blew the winds and fell on the house that, and not it fell, it had been founded for on the rock.
pieces: The rain poured down, the floods rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house. But it did not fall, because its foundation was on rock.

L.25: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded on the rock.

R.25: Rain came down, rivers flooded, and winds blew hard against that house. But it did not fall down, because it was built on rock.

decisions.choice: the rain and the rivers: winter storms and flash floods
decisions.reason: Dry stream beds could fill suddenly in the rainy season and sweep away anything built on loose ground.

decisions.choice: the storm: a picture of testing and of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 13:10-14 pictures God's judgment as a storm that brings down a badly built wall. The storm comes to both houses.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
records.gloss: And everyone the hearing of me the words these and not doing them will be likened to a man foolish, who built of him the house on the sand.
pieces: And anyone who listens to what I have said here and does not act on it will be like a foolish {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house on sand.

L.26: And everyone who hears these words of {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and does not do them will be like a foolish {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:their|his}} house on the sand.

R.26: But anyone who hears what I teach and does not obey it is like a foolish {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house on sand.

decisions.choice: hears and does not do: hearing alone is not enough
decisions.reason: Both builders heard. The difference is doing (compare James 1:22).

decisions.choice: a wise {{gender:person|man}} who built {{gender:a|his}} house
alternatives: a wise man who built his house
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the comparison applies to everyone who hears, so the inclusive form is the default.

records.source: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
records.gloss: And came down the rain and came the rivers and blew the winds and struck the house that, and it fell, and was the fall of it great.
pieces: The rain poured down, the floods rose, and the winds blew and battered that house, and it fell. And what a fall it was!"

L.27: And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell, and great was its fall."

R.27: Rain came down, rivers flooded, and winds blew hard against that house. And it fell down with a great crash."

decisions.choice: great was its fall: the sermon ends on a warning
decisions.reason: The last words leave the hearers to choose which builder they will be.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus the words these, were astonished the crowds at the teaching of him;
pieces: When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.

L.28: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, the crowds were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching,

R.28: When Jesus finished saying these things, the people were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished these words: the formula that closes each of the five long speeches
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1).

decisions.choice: the crowds: they too had heard the sermon
decisions.reason: Jesus taught his disciples (5:1-2) with the crowds listening.

records.heading: Teaching with authority

records.source: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: he was for teaching them as authority having and not as the scribes of them.
pieces: He taught them like someone with authority of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own, not like their scribes.

L.29: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

R.29: He taught with authority of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. He did not teach like their teachers of the law.

decisions.choice: authority: the right to speak for God in his own name
decisions.reason: The scribes taught by quoting the law and earlier teachers. Jesus said "But I say to you" (5:22, 28, 32, 34, 39, 44).

decisions.choice: their scribes: the scribes of the crowds
decisions.reason: "Their" sets Jesus apart from the teachers the people knew.

decisions.choice: authority of his own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast with the scribes, who taught on the authority of others.
